newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 3.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday:
* Indonesia was expected to lower import tariffs covering 1,200 product items in 1997, Bisnis Indonesia reported.
* Indonesia's export earnings from the forestry sector rose to $8.3 billion in 1996 from $7.1 billion in 1995, the official Antara news agency reported on Thursday.

* Thousands of people went on a burning and looting rampage on Thursday in the West Kalimantan district of Sanggau Ledo, the aftershock of ethnic tension that broke out Monday claiming five lives, the Jakarta Post reported.

* The Dow industrials closed with a loss of 5.78 points at 6,442.49 on Thursday after a report of robust manufacturing activity in December sparked a steep decline in the bond market, which in turn hurt stocks.
* The Jakarta composite index rose 0.67 points, or 0.11 percent, to 638.10 points in slow trading on Thursday, with the focus fixed on newly-listed light metal manufacturer Alumindo.
* On Friday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,361.75/62.75 in early trading against the opening of 2,361.80/62.30.
* Alumindo Light Metal Industry following its debut on Thursday.
* Timber firms Barito and Sumalindo on reports of an increase in Indonesia's forestry exports in 1996.
* Cement manufacturers Semen Cibinong, Indocement and Semen Gresik on reports of a possible oversupply in 1997.

* Bank Bira on reports a subsidiary of the U.S. General Electric Co had bought a seven percent stake in the bank and that it expected to post a net profit of 60 billion rupiah in 1996 against 30.34 billion rupiah last year.
